video.title: ObservationIgnored, withObservationTracking & Observations | Day 183
video.description:
Learn to explain how the Observation framework tracks changes in your models: ObservationIgnored, withObservationTracking & Observations, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ObservationIgnored - A macro that tells Observation not to track a property.
withObservationTracking - A function that runs code, then tells you when a value it read has changed.
Observations - An async sequence that gives you a new value each time a model changes.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain ObservationIgnored, withObservationTracking & Observations in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

ObservationIgnored - A macro that tells Observation not to track a property.
한국어: 옵저베이션이그노어드: 프로퍼티를 추적하지 않도록 Observation에 알려 주는 매크로

withObservationTracking - A function that runs code, then tells you when a value it read has changed.
한국어: 위드옵저베이션트래킹: 코드를 실행한 뒤 읽은 값이 바뀌면 알려 주는 함수

Observations - An async sequence that gives you a new value each time a model changes.
한국어: 옵저베이션즈: 모델이 바뀔 때마다 새 값을 주는 비동기 시퀀스

landscape.hook: Can you explain ObservationIgnored, withObservationTracking and Observations in English?

dialogue.title: Fewer extra updates

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my model has a `log` array that the view never shows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mark it with ObservationIgnored, and SwiftUI will not track it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the view does not refresh when `log` changes?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now I need to react to `n` outside a view, in plain code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use withObservationTracking. It runs a closure and tells you when a value it read has changed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it keep watching after one change?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, withObservationTracking calls its change closure only once, so you call it again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That sounds like a lot of work for many changes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Try Observations. It gives you an async sequence of values.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I can loop over Observations with await?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, each step of the loop gives you the next value of `n`.
